answers.text: Instruction: from the driver's message, always return exactly three lines in this order - drop-off time, pallet count, then any damage noted - and nothing else added on.
Tell it to list out the calls and then tell me the total number that still need a follow-up.
The finish time doesn't add up - access from 8am plus a six-hour job puts them done by early-to-mid afternoon on the 22nd itself, not finishing on the 23rd like the note says.
The invoice increase doesn't check out for me - going from 96 to 118 is around 23%, not 20% like it says here. The rest of it I'd leave for someone else to check before it's sent up.
I'd go with the second one since it shows where the 88% comes from - the actual ticket counts are there in front of you.

The second email is the one to send, it has the real volume numbers behind it. That doesn't mean the first one's wrong necessarily, it just isn't ready to send as it stands - it just needs a bit more behind it before I'd send it.
1. No, I'd leave the vendor's pricing out. 2. Yes, that's fine. 3. No, that draft isn't final. 4. Yes, that one's fine. 5. No, keep that out.
The general scope of work I think would be fine to paste as it is - it's the hourly rates, the retainer cap, and the non-disclosure part naming both companies that I'd hold back.
Before it goes out each month I check the reconciliation totals against the warehouse system - that's about as far as it goes for me.

The extraction step at the start could cause trouble if it misreads the invoice, and the step where it submits automatically is the one I'd actually put a gate on, since that's the point you can't undo.
